# Oil India Limited

<!-- Generated by `make client-docs`. Do not edit inside the markers. -->

Researched 2026-09-29 · status **complete**

Oil India Limited (OIL) is a Maharatna PSU (CIN L11101AS1959GOI001148, incorporated 1959, registered office at Duliajan, Dibrugarh district, Assam) engaged in crude oil and natural gas exploration/production. Its CSR programme is explicitly framed around 'areas of operation' rather than a standalone Northeast-priority mandate — Assam and Arunachal Pradesh feature heavily because OIL's fields, aspirational-district allotments and operational areas sit there, not because a corporate strategy document names 'Northeast India' as a target geography distinct from operations. The FY2018-19 CSR Annual Report shows total CSR spend of Rs 133.39 crore across Healthcare, Sanitation/Swachh Bharat, Education, Sustainable Livelihood, Skill Development, Capacity Building/Women, Environment, Art & Culture, Sports and Rural Infrastructure, with numerous named flagship projects (Sparsha, Arogya, Super 30, Dikhya, Rupantar, Jeevika, Swabalamban, SDI Guwahati, OIL Urja, PMUY) run in Assam and Arunachal Pradesh districts (Dibrugarh, Tinsukia, Charaideo, Miao, Manabhum/Changlang, Dhubri, Goalpara, Namsai). The FY2025-26 Annual Action Plan lists 23 board-approved projects, most explicitly scoped to 'Assam, Arunachal Pradesh, Tripura' alongside a few states outside NE (Rajasthan, Madhya Pradesh, Odisha). The community-engagement 'Sustainable Livelihood' web page gives cumulative/latest figures for Project Rupantar, Agriculture Development, and OIL Jeevika (in both Arunachal Pradesh and Assam) including beneficiary counts. No confirmed CSR project or spend figure was found for Manipur, Meghalaya, Mizoram, Nagaland or Sikkim in the sources read.

Website: https://www.oil-india.com

## Project and sector spend

- **Aspirational Districts CSR expenditure (Assam & Arunachal Pradesh)** (FY2018-19): approx Rs 15.08 crore (28% of stipulated CSR budget) across ~12 projects
  > OIL was allotted 03 districts namely Dhubri and Goalpara in Assam and Namsai in Arunachal Pradesh. Around 12 major CSR Projects with combined expenditure of approximately 15.08 Crore (which is 28% of the stipulated CSR Budget of OIL) were undertaken by OIL under key thrust areas of Education, Healthcare & Nutrition, Sanitation, and Sports for the larger benefit of people residing in the Aspirational Districts.
  <sub>OIL CSR Annual Report FY2018-19 · https://www.oil-india.com/files/expenditure_annual/OIL_CSR_English2018-19.pdf · confidence high</sub>
- **Total CSR expenditure FY2018-19** (FY2018-19): Rs 133.39 crore
  > Total 133.39 crore was the total CSR expenditure across all key thrust areas including Healthcare, Sanitation, Education, Livelihood, Skill Development and Infrastructure for FY 2018-19.
  <sub>OIL CSR Annual Report FY2018-19 · https://www.oil-india.com/files/expenditure_annual/OIL_CSR_English2018-19.pdf · confidence high</sub>

## Where the work ran

- **Geography framing: operational-area based, not a stated NE 'priority' distinct from operations**: CSR policy and vision statement tie activity to 'areas of operation' (which are concentrated in Assam/Arunachal Pradesh because that is where OIL's oil/gas fields and aspirational-district allotments are); no source read states Northeast India as a chosen strategic priority geography independent of where OIL physically operates _inferred_
  > To bring about tangible socio-economic development in operational areas of OIL, and to improve community well-being through discretionary business practices and contribution of corporate resources, as stated in OIL's CSR policy objectives.
  <sub>OIL CSR Annual Report FY2018-19 · https://www.oil-india.com/files/expenditure_annual/OIL_CSR_English2018-19.pdf · confidence medium</sub>

## Implementing partners

- **Skill Development Institute (SDI), Guwahati** (FY2018-19): Rs 1.50 crore spent FY2018-19; joint PSU initiative to skill NE youth in hydrocarbon and other trades; implementing partners IL&FS, TRTC (Ministry of MSME), Pragati Edutech
  > OIL, along with other major oil PSUs, has set up SDI at Guwahati to cater to the skilling need of youth of North East region, to enhance their employability in hydrocarbon as well as other sectors.
  <sub>OIL CSR Annual Report FY2018-19 · https://www.oil-india.com/files/expenditure_annual/OIL_CSR_English2018-19.pdf · confidence high</sub>

## Programmes

- **Agriculture Development & Village Adoption (Assam)**: 215 villages adopted; 35,157 farmers/farm families benefitting via farmers' collectives, in association with Assam Agriculture University & District Agriculture Department
  > Adopted 215 villages under 35,157 various farmers' collectives benefiting farm families, as part of the Project on Agriculture Development & Village Adoption.
  <sub>OIL community-engagement webpage · https://www.oil-india.com/community-engagement/sustainable-livelihood · confidence high</sub>
- **CSR Thrust Areas (company's own statement)**: Healthcare and Sanitation & Clean drinking water, Education, Sustainable Livelihood Generation, Capacity Building, Empowerment of Women, Skill Development, Augmentation of Rural Infrastructure, Sports and Environmental Sustainability
  > As specified under Schedule VII of the Companies Act, 2013, the company has embarked upon various CSR projects and activities under key thrust / focus areas of Healthcare and Sanitation & Clean drinking water, Education, Sustainable Livelihood Generation, Capacity Building, Empowerment of Women, Skill Development, Augmentation of Rural Infrastructure, Sports and Environmental Sustainability etc.
